newsitem.title: JAPAN: Chugoku Elec to build third reactor by 2009.
newsitem.headline: Chugoku Elec to build third reactor by 2009.

text.p: Chugoku Electric Power Co Inc said on Thursday it has notified local authorities of its plans to build a third reactor at its nuclear power plant in western Japan's Shimane Prefecture by 2009.
The electric utility plans to add a 1.37 million-kilowatt (kw) reactor to the power plant in the town of Kashima, where it already has two reactors with a combined capacity of 1.28 million kw.
Kashima mayor Kiyosumi Yamamoto said in a news conference that he intends to discuss Chugoku Electric's proposal with municipal assembly members and town residents "in a constructive manner".

Gaining the consent of local residents for construction of nuclear power plants has become increasingly difficult as a series of accidents at nuclear facilities has undermined public confidence in their safety.
A fire and explosion at a nuclear reprocessing plant at Tokaimura, 160 km northeast of Tokyo, contaminated 35 workers with minor amounts of radiation on Tuesday.

The plant is operated by state-run Power Reactor and Nuclear Fuel Development Corp (PNC), whose prototype fast-breeder reactor Monju, in Fukui Prefecture, also in western Japan, has been shut since December 1995 following a leak of sodium coolant.
Kyushu Electric Power Co Inc said earlier this week it had abandoned a plan to build a nuclear power plant in the southern Japanese city of Kushima due to local opposition.
